James Hutton is often viewed as the first modern geologist. In 1785 he presented a paper entitled Theory of the Earth to the Royal Society of Edinburgh. In his paper, he explained his theory that the Earth must be much older than had previously been supposed in order to allow enough time for mountains to be eroded and for sediments to form new rocks at the bottom of the sea, which in turn were raised up to become dry land. This antedates William Smith's geological map of England by six years, although it was constructed using a different classification of rocks.

Though Hutton believed in uniformitarianism, the idea was not widely accepted at the time.
